QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_36

question.text: SASB (Sustainability Accounting Standards Board, now part of IFRS/ISSB) differs from GRI primarily because:

answer.text: SASB indicators are industry-specific and investor-materiality focused; GRI is multi-stakeholder, broader in scope, and organised as Universal + Sector + Topic standards
SASB is a UN body; GRI is private
SASB is mandatory in India; GRI is optional
They are identical in scope and can be used interchangeably

explanation.text: The Logic: SASB (Sustainability Accounting Standards Board, now part of the IFRS Foundation through the International Sustainability Standards Board / ISSB) was designed to identify the subset of sustainability issues most likely to be financially material to investors in a specific industry, and so its standards are organised industry-by-industry around investor-materiality. GRI (Global Reporting Initiative) is designed for a broader multi-stakeholder audience (employees, communities, regulators, customers, civil society) and is organised as Universal Standards (applicable to all reporters), Sector Standards (industry-specific), and Topic Standards (specific sustainability topics). The two frameworks therefore differ mainly in audience focus (investor materiality vs multi-stakeholder) and in structure. The Trap: SASB is not a UN body and GRI is also not a UN body (it has historically collaborated with UNEP but is independent). Neither framework is mandatory in India - sustainability reporting for listed companies in India is governed by SEBI's BRSR, not by SASB or GRI directly. The two frameworks have some overlap but are not interchangeable because their audiences and materiality concepts differ. Note: The cited workbook pages (104, 147 of the Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook) mention SASB as a sustainability reporting standard and describe the GRI Universal / Sector / Topic structure, but they do not, in the pages checked, support the specific SASB industry-specific / investor-materiality framing, the IFRS / ISSB consolidation status, or the mandatory/optional claims as written. The framing above reflects general sustainability-reporting practice and the publicly disclosed positioning of SASB and GRI.
